tokyo_kacchan_tempura_ueno.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: a tempura stand (wheat batter); the alternative set is oden.
tokyo_kacchan_tempura_ueno.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the tempura set includes shrimp and the tempura is served with tentsuyu; the other set is oden.
tokyo_kacchan_tempura_ueno.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–21:45 (last order 21:30); open all year (Tabelog). No reservations; phone may not be answered while open. Standing only, about 20 places. Non-smoking; smoking outside only. Cash only (no cards, e-money or QR). 60-minute limit on the senbero set (April and October 2026 reviews). Opened 31 March 2010 (Tabelog).
tokyo_kacchan_tempura_ueno.notes: [Standing tempura bar · Ueno, the dice senbero under the tracks] A busy stand-up bar under the railway between Ueno and Okachimachi, at the Ameyoko entrance, open from 11 am. Hand over ¥1,300 and you get four dice in a wooden masu: spend them on up to four drinks (a sour is one die, a beer two) and receive a plate of freshly fried tempura — shrimp, eggplant, lotus root, pumpkin and more — or an oden set instead. Extras like conger-eel tempura cost more. Diners in October 2026 loved the crisp tempura, the friendly crowd and the value, but note the drinks are on the light side and there is a 60-minute limit when it's busy; one reviewer paid ¥1,400. Standing only, cash only.

chef_bio.background: A corporate-member Tabelog listing; no source names the operator, owner or cook.
chef_bio.specialty: Senbero set of tempura and four drinks.

anecdotes.text: "When you hand over JPY 1,300, you receive four dice, and you can order your favorite drinks based on the dice rolls… All the drinks are a bit on the lighter side." — October 2026.
"The tempura included shrimp, potato, pumpkin, eggplant, and lotus root. The cost performance is excellent, and the tempura is freshly fried, crispy, and delicious!" — October 2026.
"Although the 60-minute time limit felt a bit rushed, I managed to finish all my drinks within the time." — April 2026.

tokyo_katsuretsu_takeda_yotsuya.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: a cutlet house where nearly every main is breaded and fried (pork, chicken and tenderloin cutlets, croquettes, fries), with demi-glace and curry sauces. The butter-grilled scallops or oysters and pork ginger are not breaded, but the sauces are not described.
tokyo_katsuretsu_takeda_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: every set is built on pork, beef, chicken or seafood; rice, shredded cabbage and pickles are the only plant items.
tokyo_katsuretsu_takeda_yotsuya.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:00–15:30 (last order 15:00) and 17:00–21:00 (last order 20:30); Sat 11:00–15:30 (last order 15:00); closed Sunday, holidays, Obon and New Year (Tabelog). No reservations; expect a line: 20–40 minutes is common, a Saturday diner waited 2 hours in March 2026, and in October 2026 one diner was 12th in line at 10:50 and still got in at opening. Cash or PayPay only, PayPay since the end of 2025 (Tabelog; January 2026 review). Order by voice, pay after (October 2026). 13 seats: two counters and two tables for two; non-smoking; takeaway (Tabelog). Children welcome (Tabelog). Opened 26 September 2011 per Tabelog; TV Tokyo says the shop reopened as Takeda two days after Elise closed, giving Elise's run as 1970–2009.
tokyo_katsuretsu_takeda_yotsuya.notes: [Yoshoku · Yotsuya, a cutlet diner with a line at the station crossing] A 13-seat Showa-style Western diner at the Yotsuya-mitsuke crossing, on Tabelog's Diner or Teishoku 100 list in 2021, 2024 and 2026, and almost always with a line outside. TV Tokyo tells its story: from 1970 the spot was Elise, a yoshoku restaurant loved by 上智大学 students, which closed one day without warning and reopened two days later as Takeda, keeping Elise favourites such as the winter butter-grilled oyster set; a Tabelog user's roundup says Elise was opened by the second generation of a business founded in Tsukiji and that the third generation turned it into this cutlet shop. The house cutlet is a thick aged Mochibuta loin under demi-glace and grated Edam; crab cream croquettes are the add-on reviewers mention most, and autumn brings butter-grilled scallops before the oysters. In October 2026 the Elise beef tomato returned for a limited time. Three cooks behind the counter, signatures of TV crews and celebrities on the walls. Cash or PayPay; no bookings; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.origin: TV Tokyo (アド街ック天国, 14 November 2020): the shop was the yoshoku restaurant エリーゼ from 1970 to 2009, closed without notice and reopened two days later as たけだ. Tabelog gives the opening date as 26 September 2011.
chef_bio.background: No source names the owner or cooks. A Tabelog user's roundup (matome 27344) about 洋食エリーゼ えいすけ in Mizuho-dai says the business was founded in Tsukiji, the second generation opened 洋食エリーゼ in Yotsuya, the third generation converted it into this katsuretsu shop, and a cook who trained alongside the third generation, 佐藤氏, opened えいすけ. An October 2026 diner notes that えいすけ's menu calls the beef tomato the most popular dish at "Yotsuya Elise". An October 2026 diner counted three staff in the kitchen and saw TV and celebrity signatures on the walls. Tabelog Diner "Tabelog 100" 2024 and 2026; Teishoku "Tabelog 100" 2021.
chef_bio.specialty: Pork katsuretsu with demi-glace and Edam; crab cream croquette; winter butter-grilled oysters.

anecdotes.text: "Once again, I had to wait 2 hours… I guess it's to be expected on a Saturday… it's a monthly treat for me, so I don't mind waiting." — March 2026, a 14th visit.
"This time, I decided to try the Beef Tomato, a revival dish from the Elise era. - Beef Tomato Set Meal (JPY 1500)" — October 2026.
"The interior has a retro Western-style diner vibe reminiscent of the Showa era… The walls are adorned with signatures from TV shows and various celebrities." — October 2026, pork ginger set.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: テレビ東京「出没！アド街ック天国」(2020年11月14日、四谷): かつれつ 四谷たけだ、揚げ物メニューがメイン、1970年から2009年までは「エリーゼ」という人気の洋食屋、上智大生に愛された「エリーゼ」は予告なく閉店し、2日後に「たけだ」として再オープン、冬季限定の「カキバター焼定食」などエリーゼ時代の人気メニューの一部は今も健在、四谷1-4-2 峯村ビル1F。食べログまとめ (ユーザー): えいすけはもともと築地で創業、二代目が四ツ谷に「洋食エリーゼ」を開業、三代目がカツレツ専門店「かつれつ四谷たけだ」に業態転換、三代目と修行をともにした佐藤氏が「えいすけ」を開業。食べログ (店舗会員): 食堂百名店2024・2026、定食百名店2021、月〜金11:00〜15:30・17:00〜21:00、土11:00〜15:30、日祝休み、予約不可、カード・電子マネー不可、PayPay 可、13席、禁煙、2011年9月26日オープン、ポークかつれつ定食1,680円 (デミグラスとエダムチーズ)、カニクリームコロッケ定食1,300円。口コミ(2026年1月〜10月): 行列、ビーフトマト定食、カニクリームコロッケ1個480円、ホタテバター焼定食1,800円、カキは11月から、厨房に3人、壁にサイン。

tokyo_spaghetti_nagai_yotsuya.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: a spaghetti shop; every main is wheat pasta, and several sauces are soy-sauce based.
tokyo_spaghetti_nagai_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Ask. Most spaghetti carries cod roe, seafood, bacon, sausage, tuna, egg or cream; a garlic sauce with basil exists, but the one reviewed came with clams. The mini salad is the plant dish named.
tokyo_spaghetti_nagai_yotsuya.hours_raw: Mon–Sat and holidays 11:30–20:00, no afternoon break; may close early some days; closed Sunday, with occasional Sunday openings (Tabelog). No reservations; a line at lunch (30–40 minutes once in September 2026), quiet mid-afternoon (2025–26 reviews). Cash only (Tabelog). 16 seats: an L-shaped counter of 6 and tables (2×4, 1×2); up stairs on the 2nd floor, with no sign outside (Tabelog; October 2026 review). Non-smoking (Tabelog).
tokyo_spaghetti_nagai_yotsuya.notes: [Pasta · Yotsuya, a one-cook spaghetti counter up the stairs] No sign outside: climb to the second floor of an old building on Shinmichi-dōri and you find an L-shaped counter, a few tables and walls of bookshelves, with Western rock playing softly. Diners place it in the Hashiya line of Japanese-style spaghetti: thick-ish noodles served piping hot, cod roe with squid and shiso, a soy-sauce egg and bacon "carbonara" one diner likened to tamago kake gohan, seafood in a tomato sauce that is not sweet, and meat sauce with tuna. A diner on a sixth visit in September 2026 says the cook works alone yet keeps waits short; one diner called the owner a book-loving craftsman, and an October 2026 diner came for the carbonara that, in the diner's words, Gentosha's Kenjo loves. The woman out front struck two 2026 diners as curt, and one found the pasta ordinary. Open straight through from 11:30 to 20:00, so mid-afternoon has no line; cash only; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: No source names the owner (one September 2026 diner wrote "Mr. Nagai?" as a guess). Reviews place the shop in the "Hashiya" lineage of Japanese-style spaghetti (September 2026, two reviewers).
chef_bio.specialty: Cod roe and squid; egg and bacon in soy sauce; seafood tomato.

anecdotes.text: "It is well-known as a prestigious establishment that follows the famous 'Hashiya' lineage of spaghetti… Although the chef operates solo, [the chef] works efficiently, ensuring minimal wait times." — September 2026, a sixth visit.

tokyo_kakurega_dining_saate_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask. Steak, churrasco and roast meats are the core, but sauces are not described; much else is wheat-based or fried (kara-age, croquettes, garlic toast, pasta, naan, croutons on the Caesar).
tokyo_kakurega_dining_saate_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Ask. The listing ticks "Vegetarian options"; edamame, salads, fresh spring rolls and fries are on the menu, but nothing is marked vegan and the courses centre on meat.
tokyo_kakurega_dining_saate_yotsuya.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:00–23:30 (last order 23:00); Sunday only for booked groups of five or more, by phone by the day before (Tabelog). No cover charge (Tabelog). 45 seats, curtained semi-private rooms for 4 to 20, whole-floor hire for 35–50; smoking allowed except at lunch; children not admitted at dinner (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB) and QR including PayPay, Alipay and WeChat Pay; no e-money (Tabelog). Same-day bookings welcome (June 2026 review).
tokyo_kakurega_dining_saate_yotsuya.notes: [Izakaya · Yotsuya, a meat bar with curtained booths] A second-floor dining bar at the mouth of Shinmichi-dōri, a minute from the station, whose sign in Latin letters confused one returning diner. Curtains split the 45 seats into semi-private booths, and the menu leans Western: sizzling steak on a hot plate, churrasco, house roast beef and roast pork, kara-age, ajillo with bread, garlic toast, fried rice to finish. Most 2026 visitors came for the cheap drinks courses, from about ¥3,000 for two hours with nine dishes up to a three-hour meat course with wagyu steak and all-you-can-eat fried chicken and fries; one Saturday night in August 2026 the place was nearly empty. Open from 11:00 every day but Sunday (groups by booking only); smoking allowed at night, no children at dinner.

tokyo_kaiseki_oui_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask when booking: the official site says "アレルギー等ご相談くださいませ" (consult us about allergies). Courses include sashimi with sweet soy sauce, sukiyaki, battered fried dishes, soba as a finish and chocolate cake (2025–26 reviews).
tokyo_kaiseki_oui_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: dashi-led kaiseki; the courses include fish, wagyu and chicken.
tokyo_kaiseki_oui_yotsuya.hours_raw: Tue–Sat lunch 11:30–14:00, dinner 17:30–22:00 (last seating 20:00); Sunday lunch only; closed Monday, holidays and over New Year (Tabelog; official site). Reservations advised (lunch was full twice for one January 2026 diner); same-day cancellations charged in full (Tabelog). Dinner can also be à la carte (April 2026). 10 seats: 6 at the counter facing the open kitchen and one semi-private room for up to 4; non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Children welcome; takeaway (Tabelog). Opened 8 October 2020; the site marked its 6th anniversary on 8 October 2026.
tokyo_kaiseki_oui_yotsuya.notes: [Kaiseki · Yotsuya, a six-seat counter down a lane] Down a narrow lane off Shinjuku-dōri, a quiet Japanese room with six counter seats facing the open kitchen and one small semi-private room, opened in 2020 and run by 宮島央一, an owner-chef who, the site says, drew on time abroad to train in creative kaiseki, sushi and Italian kitchens. Courses change daily: sashimi with a sweet soy sauce, a grilled fish such as Lake Biwa ayu, a fried course, A5 wagyu as sukiyaki or steak, and rice cooked in a clay pot, whose leftovers come back as onigiri to take home; the rich chocolate cake at the end astonished one diner. Lunch from ¥3,000 is the way in and books up, and dinner runs ¥7,950–13,000, or à la carte. One diner says the name comes from Hokusai. Closed Mondays and holidays; Sunday lunch only.

roles: Owner-chef (official site: "店主 宮島央一")
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: drawing on experience abroad, trained at shops of many genres, chiefly creative Japanese and kaiseki, sushi and Italian; "色々経験した分、誰にも真似できないと思って" (having experienced so much, no one else can copy it). Tabelog: "our chef, who has experience in both Japanese and Italian cuisine"; an August 2026 diner learned that the chef had worked in Italian cuisine. Opened 8 October 2020 (Tabelog; the site's anniversary notices). The site lists Tabelog and 一休.com bookings and an online store.
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal ingredients chosen with care and served as courses; inventive dishes from an owner unbound by convention (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal kaiseki; A5 beef sukiyaki; clay-pot takikomi gohan.

anecdotes.text: "The rice was cooked in a clay pot, and even though it was too much for two people to finish, I appreciated that they made it into onigiri for us to take home!" — July 2025, lunch.
"Lunch kaiseki for JPY 3,000, tax included. A cozy restaurant with 6 counter seats and private rooms… The name is indeed derived from Hokusai." — November 2025.
"The sukiyaki had a refined balance, not too sweet… and at JPY 2000, it was an incredible value." — April 2026, à la carte after a walk at Chidorigafuchi.

tokyo_roppongi_chotto.gf_detail: Ask. Nothing is called gluten-free. The long menu includes homemade gyoza, fried fish, sweet-and-spicy konnyaku, butter-and-soy teppan vegetables and soy-grilled rice balls (2024–2025 reviews).
tokyo_roppongi_chotto.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish-and-skewer izakaya; vegetable dishes such as the mixed butter teppan use butter and soy, and the appetizer has been oden.
tokyo_roppongi_chotto.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 18:15–23:30; Sat 18:30–22:30; holidays 18:15–22:30; closed Sundays; hours may change (Tabelog). Cash only (Tabelog; July 2025). Book ahead — it is often full (June 2024, July 2025). Smoking allowed; no children (Tabelog). 20 seats, counter and tables, up an elevated floor reached by a small path (May 2026).
tokyo_roppongi_chotto.notes: [Izakaya · Roppongi, a couple-run Showa izakaya] Up a narrow way to the second floor of an old building a minute from Roppongi crossing, a 20-seat izakaya that reviewers describe as run by a couple, with a retro Showa feel, a TV in the corner and a menu so long it is hard to choose. The cook — the elderly gentleman in the kitchen, as one January 2026 diner put it — makes almost everything single-handed: sizzling homemade gyoza on a hot plate, fried mehikari, butter-and-soy teppan vegetables, satsuma-age, eel-liver skewers, sashimi and daily specials, most around ¥800. Prices are low for Roppongi (about ¥3,500 a head in October 2025), the shochu is poured strong, and it fills with office workers, so book. Cash only; smoking allowed; no children; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Reviewers describe the izakaya as run by a couple: "A Showa-era style izakaya run by a couple" and the wife's enthusiastic service (July 2025); "this cozy izakaya run by a couple" (October 2025); "the elderly gentleman in the kitchen" (January 2026); "the chef prepares almost everything by himself" and a chat "with the master and the owner" (May 2026). No one is named in the sources read.
chef_bio.specialty: Homemade gyoza; long Showa izakaya menu.

anecdotes.text: "Six large gyoza filled with a generous amount of stuffing! Served sizzling hot on a teppan." — October 2025, homemade gyoza ¥800.
"The coffee liqueur is homemade and usually only served to regular customers... I'm grateful for that." — May 2026.
"The retro Showa-style interior really lifts the spirits. It's like being in a theme park!" — June 2024.

tokyo_kunpu_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. Nothing is called gluten-free; every course ends with the house fresh-baked bread, and dishes have included chicken tempura, chijimi and a mapo tofu bowl (2025–2026 reviews).
tokyo_kunpu_roppongi.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog ticks "vegetarian options" and the shop invites you to name what you want to eat, but courses centre on fish, meat and cheese.
tokyo_kunpu_roppongi.hours_raw: From 18:00, usually to about 24:00 (Tabelog says sometimes as late as 05:00; the official site says until 24:00, and earlier starts by arrangement). Closed Sundays and holidays (Tabelog); the official site also lists Saturdays as closed, with weekend and holiday hire for 20 or more. December: open every day until the 30th; reopens 3 January (Tabelog). No service charge. 100 seats, all semi-private, divided by roll screens (official site; a June 2026 diner could hear the next table); half the room (30 seats) can be hired for ¥30,000. Non-smoking. Cards and QR. Children welcome, with a kids' menu. Opened 1 September 1999 (Tabelog).
tokyo_kunpu_roppongi.notes: [Izakaya · Roppongi, all-in courses with premium shochu and fresh bread] On the second floor along Roppongi-dori, a 100-seat restaurant of semi-private tables divided by roll screens, open since 1999. Courses include the drinks — and they are serious ones: Juyondai sake, Moriizo, Maou and Murao shochu, Yamazaki and Ichiro's Malt whisky — while beer and highball glasses grow bigger with every refill. The food is "sosaku" (creative) Japanese-Western cooking made fresh, with a Caesar salad tossed at the table under shaved cheese and fresh-baked bread with honey to finish every course; a July 2026 business dinner featured Oita fish and Bungo beef. Diners call the drinks a bargain; one in June 2026 found the food plainer than expected and the screens thin, and one notes the owner's strong personality. Mostly for groups; closed Sundays and holidays (and Saturdays, per the shop's site).

chef_bio.background: Opened 1 September 1999 (Tabelog). The official site promises nothing frozen or made in advance, premium drinks at nearly cost, and drinks you request a week ahead. A December 2025 reviewer mentions the owner's strong personality; a July 2026 diner notes turmeric drinks and tablets on the table. No one is named in the sources read.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Tell us what you want to eat" — written on the menu since opening (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Premium all-you-can-drink courses; table-side Caesar salad; fresh-baked bread.

anecdotes.text: "To my surprise, they serve the renowned Junmai Daiginjo sake, Juyondai, in generous pours. The all-you-can-drink option at JPY 5,000 raises questions about how they can offer such value." — December 2025.
"The signature dish here is the Caesar salad, prepared right in front of you." — May 2026.
"The seating is separated by a curtain, so I could hear everything from the neighboring table quite clearly." — June 2026.

tokyo_yelo_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. Shaved ice with syrups and milk sauces may avoid wheat, but nothing is called gluten-free and toppings such as tiramisu (with cocoa and mascarpone) and the hot dogs are not described.
tokyo_yelo_roppongi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the kakigori are built on fresh milk sauces, with mascarpone and cream toppings (official site; 2026 reviews).
tokyo_yelo_roppongi.hours_raw: Mon–Thu 11:00–02:00; Fri 11:00–05:00; Sat 11:30–05:00; Sun 11:30–02:00; to 05:00 on weekdays in summer; hours change by season — check the shop's X account (Tabelog; official site). No reservations; a paid TableCheck FastPass for priority entry in summer (official site); long summer queues (2020 review). 16 seats: 6 at the counter and five tables for two. Non-smoking. Cards, IC/e-money and QR. Children welcome. English menu. Self-service water and rooibos tea. Opened 1 April 2014 (Tabelog).
tokyo_yelo_roppongi.notes: [Kakigori · Roppongi, shaved ice until the small hours] A small kakigori bar three minutes from Roppongi Station that serves shaved ice all year and late into the night — to 2 am most days and 5 am at weekends. The ice is pure, temperature-controlled and shaved fine, under house syrups and fresh milk sauces; the tiramisu kakigori with extra mascarpone foam is the favourite (about ¥1,500 in 2026), with pistachio, mango and seasonal flavours, plus "night kakigori" spiked with alcohol such as rum raisin. The same shop runs Amber for hot dogs and hot sandwiches. Reviews in 2026 range from "Japan's best" to "average", and one late-night diner found the second bowl crunchy; summer brings queues (a paid FastPass is offered). Self-service water and rooibos.

chef_bio.background: Opened 1 April 2014 (Tabelog). The official site presents yelo (kakigori) with Amber (hot dogs and hot sandwiches), whose sausages come from a workshop keeping to traditional German methods and whose bread was developed with a well-known baker.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Light and healthy, yet as satisfying as any sweet" — pure ice kept at the right temperature for a fine, melting texture, with homemade syrups and fresh milk sauce, to enjoy all year (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Tiramisu kakigori; night kakigori.

anecdotes.text: "I've visited over 50 kakigori shops across the country, and this one is truly the best!" — August 2026.
"I visited around 1:30 AM and was surprised to find the place completely empty!… the second order of strawberry was quite crunchy." — September 2026.
"I definitely recommend adding the espuma! For just JPY 200, it’s worth adding to everything." — September 2026, tiramisu ¥1,300 and pistachio ¥1,400.

tokyo_go_tsubo_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. Raw, steamed and grilled oysters are served simply, but nothing is called gluten-free and side dishes include uni butter toast and a salted-cod-roe baked potato (2026 reviews).
tokyo_go_tsubo_roppongi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: an oyster bar; side dishes include bacon, mussels, cod roe and sea urchin.
tokyo_go_tsubo_roppongi.hours_raw: From 18:00; closes when the day's oysters run out (July 2026); hours and closing days may change (Tabelog). The closing time here is a placeholder. Cash only (Tabelog; September 2026). A one-person operation — book by phone right after opening or later in the evening, say how many oysters you want, and order all at once (September 2026). No glasses for water; buy a bottle from the vending machine downstairs (September 2026). 14 counter seats; smoking allowed (Tabelog).
tokyo_go_tsubo_roppongi.notes: [Oysters · Roppongi, a one-man oyster bar at ¥250 a piece] On the fourth floor of a back-street building, a 14-seat counter with doodles on the walls and a blackboard crammed with dishes, where the owner alone shucks, steams and grills oysters at about ¥250 apiece — Akkeshi oysters in July 2026, and one July 2026 diner ate about 20. Order them raw, steamed (the favourite of several reviewers) or grilled, add uni butter toast or a cod-roe baked potato, and drink wine by the bottle; around ¥6,000 a head with plenty of drinking. It is cash only, there are no water glasses (buy a bottle downstairs), smoking is allowed, and when the oysters run out the night is over — so book by phone, say how many oysters you want, and order everything early. One diner noted the view over a cemetery.

chef_bio.background: A September 2026 reviewer who first came seven years earlier writes that "the owner manages everything by himself"; another September 2026 diner calls it "a one-person operation". No one is named in the sources read.
chef_bio.specialty: Oysters raw, steamed or grilled at about ¥250 each; uni butter toast.

anecdotes.text: "The oysters are only JPY 250 each and incredibly delicious, so it’s easy to overindulge!" — September 2026: 12 raw, 4 grilled and 14 steamed for the table.
"When I asked for a chaser of water, I was told, 'We don’t have glasses, so please buy a bottle from the vending machine downstairs.'" — September 2026.
"Eating oysters while looking at the cemetery was an interesting experience." — July 2026.

tokyo_hi_no_buta_ningyocho.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: thick wheat noodles in a Jiro-style bowl.
tokyo_hi_no_buta_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: tonkotsu broth, pork chashu and a meat mapo sauce on the Fusion.
tokyo_hi_no_buta_ningyocho.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:00–15:00 and 17:30–21:00 (last order 20:45); Sun 11:00–15:00 (last order 14:45); hours may change (Tabelog). Buy a ticket and pay by PayPay — no cards or e-money (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). 7 counter seats, cramped (September 2026). The shop asks queuers not to block the neighbours' doors or the apartment entrance and to fold back at "Kamiya" (Tabelog). Delivery riders pick up orders (October 2026). Opened 26 February 2018 (Tabelog).
tokyo_hi_no_buta_ningyocho.notes: [Ramen · Ningyocho, a Jiro-meets-Nakamoto bowl at a 7-seat counter] Ningyocho's only Jiro-style ramen shop (September 2026), seven cramped counter stools a minute from exit A5. The owner trained at both Ramen Jiro and Nakamoto (nlab, 2018; July 2026 review) and fused them in the house "Fusion": a mountain of bean sprouts and thick pork over thick noodles, crowned with spicy mapo tofu. Call garlic, ginger and extra vegetables when asked. The plain ramen (¥950) and dry noodles are there too, plus a rotating limited bowl — chilled noodles in summer, a yakisoba bowl in October 2026. Opinions split. Fans praise the thick tender pork and the mapo, while October 2026 diners found the broth weak and the noodles thinner and drier than they remembered. Two September and October 2026 diners found the service curt. Expect a short queue at lunch; PayPay only. The head shop is in Kuki, Saitama, and this one is directly run.

roles: Owner (unnamed; trained at Ramen Jiro and Nakamoto, per nlab 2018 and a July 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: Per nlab (ITmedia), 30 March 2018: the head shop is 蒙麺火の豚 in Kuki, Saitama; the Ningyocho shop is directly run, not a franchise; the owner trained at both Jiro and Nakamoto; the "Fusion" is the signature. Opened 26 February 2018 (Tabelog). An October 2026 diner who had not visited for four years found the niboshi ramen gone and limited bowls rotating.
chef_bio.specialty: The Fusion: Jiro-style ramen with Nakamoto-style mapo.

anecdotes.text: "The 'Fusion' combines Jiro-style with Mongolian flavors, featuring a small amount of tofu on top of bean sprouts, covered in a spicy mapo tofu sauce." — September 2026, ¥1,050.
"However, even after mixing it well, the flavor was weak and lacked richness." — October 2026, ramen ¥950.
"The pork was thick and tender—so tasty!" — July 2026, Fusion ¥1,000, tenth visit.

tokyo_menya_oto_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a dried-sardine (niboshi) broth with pork chashu.
tokyo_menya_oto_ningyocho.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–22:30; closed only over the New Year (Tabelog). Regular, large or extra noodles at no extra charge, and a free topping that changes by weekday (August–October 2026). Opened 15 June 2023 (Tabelog).
tokyo_menya_oto_ningyocho.notes: [Ramen · Ningyocho, niboshi ramen from a Kitasenju favourite] A ten-seat counter two minutes from Ningyocho station, the branch of a popular Kitasenju niboshi shop (Tabelog), open every day from 11:00 to 22:30. Two soups to choose from. The light niboshi soba (¥890) is a clean soy-sauce bowl that one August 2026 diner found barely tasted of sardine. The original rich niboshi ramen (¥990) is cement-grey but, reviewers say, balanced rather than overpowering. Both come with thin, straight house-made noodles that snap when bitten, chashu, menma and yuzu peel. A larger portion or extra noodles cost nothing, and there's a free topping that changes by day. Cash only via a ticket machine. One August 2026 diner was put off by stained paper aprons.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog's shop text: the main store in Kitasenju is a popular spot (Tabelog 3.69); soup crafted by skilled artisans over three days; house-made noodles without preservatives; the social-media account is shared across all locations. Opened 15 June 2023 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Light and rich niboshi ramen; house-made noodles.

anecdotes.text: "The broth had the characteristic grayish hue of niboshi (dried sardines), but it wasn't the overly thick and rich type." — October 2026, original rich niboshi ramen ¥990.
"The broth was a light soy sauce flavor, and I didn't really taste the niboshi (dried sardines)." — August 2026, seasoned-egg light niboshi soba ¥990.
"When I requested a paper apron, the first one had stains that looked like soup splatters." — August 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 麺屋 音 人形町店、ラーメン、つけ麺、日本橋人形町2-6-12、人形町駅A3出口から徒歩2分、毎日11:00〜22:30 (年末年始以外)、予約不可、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、10席、禁煙、子ども可、2023年6月15日オープン、Kitasenju の本店は食べログ3.69、3日かけて作るスープ、無添加の自家製麺、SNSは全店共通。メニュー (2026年9月): 淡麗煮干しそば890円、味玉990円、特製1,290円、元祖濃厚煮干しそば990円、味玉1,090円、特製1,290円、手揉み中華そば950円、煮干し油そば890円〜1,190円。口コミ(2026年7月〜10月): セメントのような灰色の濃厚煮干し、濃すぎずバランスが良い、淡麗は醤油が前に出て煮干しは弱いという声、細いストレートの自家製麺、並・大盛り・替え玉無料、曜日ごとのトッピングサービス、紙エプロンの汚れが気になったという声も。

tokyo_katsu_yoshi_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a pork tonkatsu restaurant.
tokyo_katsu_yoshi_ningyocho.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:30–14:00 and 17:30–20:30; closed Sunday; hours may change (Tabelog). Reservations accepted and advised — a line forms before 11:30 on weekdays, and phones can be hard to get through (October 2026). Cards (JCB, AMEX, Diners only); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 19 seats: 7 at the ground-floor counter in front of the fryer, 12 at tables upstairs (Tabelog). Non-smoking. In a renovated old house down an alley (October 2026). Opened 1 November 2016 (Tabelog).
tokyo_katsu_yoshi_ningyocho.notes: [Tonkatsu · Ningyocho, a celebrated tonkatsu counter in a renovated house] A tonkatsu restaurant in a renovated old house down an alley near Ningyocho station, on Tabelog's Tonkatsu 100 list six times between 2018 and 2026. Sit at the seven-seat counter downstairs to watch each cutlet breaded and fried; tables are upstairs. Loin and fillet cost the same by weight (¥1,925 for 110 g in October 2026), with rice and nuka pickles ordered separately and refilled free. The meat comes rosy, tender and sweet-fatted under a light crust, eaten with salt, plum salt, sauce or wasabi soy. A ¥4,950 course adds a croquette, simmered fillet and a soft-shell-turtle curry to pour over the last of the katsu. Book: a line forms before opening. One October 2026 diner found the batter heavier than before. Closed Sundays.

Cards; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 8 seats at an L-shaped counter; second floor, stairs only (Tabelog; April 2026). Non-smoking. Opened 16 May 2023 (September 2026 review).
tokyo_sushi_koike_ningyocho.notes: [Sushi · Ningyocho, an eight-seat counter with a ¥3,850 sushi lunch] Up a flight of stairs behind the Ningyocho crossing, an eight-seat L-shaped counter opened in 2023 by a chef from a sushi bar near Marunouchi's Nijubashi (September 2026). The cheerful chef and the warmth of the room keep diners coming back; one has been 31 times. The draw is lunch. For ¥3,850 the "usual" brings chawanmushi, tamagoyaki, about eight thick-cut nigiri on generous rice, a mini eel bowl, miso soup and a negitoro roll. It books out about a month ahead, so reserve on Ikkyu. Dinner is a ¥12,100 nigiri course or a ¥16,500 omakase heavy on small dishes for sake drinkers. A June 2026 regular says it lacks high-end finesse but shines on value. Lunch Wednesday to Sunday; closed Mondays.

tokyo_gg_kuramae_ecute_ueno.notes: [Café · inside Ueno Station, coffee in a bear bottle] A tiny café inside the JR Ueno ticket gates, the station branch of a Kuramae coffee and bar, opened in April 2025. Its draw is the bear-shaped "Kuma bottle": lattes, matcha latte and teas come in a resealable bear you can rinse and take home (about ¥850 with a drink in 2026), alongside regular cups from ¥700. Food is light — the cheesecake from the Kuramae shop, scones and honey-butter toast on Pelican bread — and the shelves sell bear-themed goods. With about ten seats it is often full; one September 2026 diner found the scones reheated rather than freshly baked as advertised. Card, IC and PayPay.

Diners in 2026 praise the noodles and the kind owner, who works alone; one diner found it not the cleanest, another the noodles a bit soft. Closed weekends.

tokyo_mendokoro_kaishin_roppongi.notes: [Ramen · Roppongi, clam shio ramen by the crossing until dawn] A 19-seat ramen shop right at Roppongi crossing that stays open from 11:30 am until 6:30 or 7 the next morning. There is a chicken shoyu ramen too, which a returning diner found less special than the clam bowl. Reviewers in 2026 note friendly staff from overseas, slow service on a training night, and a mobile ordering step if you pay by card. A reviewer believes the shop was earlier called Tsunagu.

tokyo_mezzo_roppongi.notes: [Bar · Roppongi, a DJ bar with food until 5 am] A minute from Roppongi crossing, a two-floor bar: downstairs a casual bar with a DJ booth and a terrace, upstairs a marble-and-black lounge with sofas and private rooms for parties. Drinks are cheap early (¥500 until 9 pm in September 2025) and there is a proper food menu — fried chicken, carbonara, pizza, rice croquettes and a photogenic wagyu tamago-kake-gohan. tokyo_kicko_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. Nothing is called gluten-free; the courses mix nigiri with dashi-based kaiseki dishes, Shaoxing-wine-marinated shrimp, tempura, fried cod roe and soy-based seasoning (2025–2026 reviews).

tokyo_kicko_roppongi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat and days around holidays 18:00–23:00 (last order 22:00); closed Sundays and holidays; also irregular closures (Tabelog). Reservation only; same-day bookings by phone only; same-day cancellations charged the full course. Prices include a 10% service charge; no cover. 8 seats: a hinoki counter of 4 and a private room for 4. Heated tobacco only in the private room. Cards; no e-money or QR. English menu; English- and Chinese-speaking staff. Children welcome; a children's menu from ¥5,000 by reservation (Tabelog).
tokyo_kicko_roppongi.notes: [Sushi · Roppongi, a sushi kaiseki from an owner-chef with a past in China and Okinawa] A long-running Roppongi obanzai kaiseki turned sushi kaiseki in 2023 under owner-chef 笠井 (Kasai, as Tabelog writes it), with a hinoki counter of four and a private room for four. The chef, from Muroran per a 2025 diner, has cooked in China and Okinawa, and courses mix small kaiseki plates — botan shrimp in Shaoxing wine, a hairy-crab chawanmushi with homemade karasumi, oden in autumn, sometimes whale — with nigiri on lightly red-vinegared rice, ending in a crab-and-sea-urchin risotto. Courses run from about ¥15,000 to ¥28,000 including service. Diners in 2025–2026 found the chef gruff at first and warm once talking; one heard a newcomer scolded behind the scenes. English- and Chinese-speaking staff; heated tobacco only in the private room.

tokyo_sushi_shishido_roppongi.notes: [Sushi · Roppongi, an Edomae omakase that runs until 5 am] A sleek black counter of ten, four minutes from Roppongi Station, that opened in August 2026 and serves an Edomae omakase from 6 pm to 5 am. The chef has 18 years of experience, including work in Taiwan and Malaysia (shop text), and a September 2026 diner says the chef has opened sushi shops overseas. The ¥30,000 course runs to about 16–18 plates mixing nigiri — chutoro, otoro, marinated akami, sweet shrimp, seared sardine — with cooked dishes such as grilled swordfish, a white-fish meunière with Japanese salsa and a showpiece of salmon roe, sea urchin and caviar; a ¥50,000 special course uses finer fish. Diners in 2026 praise a friendly chef and generous portions; late at night it doubles as a karaoke bar.
